title: Allow large pending publish byte thresholds
summary: Allow pending-publish autonomy byte thresholds to load as 64-bit runtime config values so drain startup does not fail on valid large byte defaults.
reason: Live pending-publish drain could not start because AutonomyPendingTotalReviewBytes was validated as a valid large integer but then passed through a 32-bit runtime getter.
behavior_before: MediaPipeline.ps1 startup failed when loading valid 64-bit pending-publish byte thresholds such as 107374182400.
behavior_after: Runtime config resolves those byte thresholds through a 64-bit getter and exposes them in the resolved config dump.
manual_validation: Live MediaPipeline.ps1 -DrainPendingPushes completed: 89 attempted, 89 succeeded, 0 errors; PendingServerPush empty after verified stale-manifest backup cleanup
git diff --check on touched paths - passed
rollback_plan: Revert the Get-ConfigInt64 runtime config changes and test/dump assertions. If a stale manifest backup must be restored, copy the backed up manifest from E:\Videos\Scratch\State\Progress\stale_pending_manifest_backups back to PendingServerPush only if the corresponding payload is restored first.
notes:
Add 64-bit runtime config getter for byte thresholds.
Expose the large pending-publish byte thresholds in the resolved config dump.
Root cause was runtime config loading 64-bit pending-publish byte thresholds through Int32, preventing drain startup.
